signals.detail: A relay announced itself as "paypal.com" but the receiving server resolved the connection back to "unknown.badhost.example" (203.0.113.9). The sending machine is not what it claimed to be.

args.line: Received: from internal (internal [10.1.2.3]) by mx.recipient.example with SMTP id z; Mon, 1 Jan 2024 10:00:00 +0000

signals.detail: The only recorded hop came from 10.1.2.3, a private/internal address. For mail claiming to be from an outside organization, that means it was injected inside a network rather than delivered across the internet.

Received: from a.example (a.example [203.0.113.1]) by b.example with ESMTP id t2; Mon, 1 Jan 2024 12:00:00 +0000

signals.label: Forged Delivery Path
signals.detail: Timestamps in the Received chain run backwards: a later hop is dated before an earlier one. Servers cannot rewrite the clocks of servers further down the path, so at least one of these headers was fabricated.
